name: Amira Lam
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I bought my first suit with a refund from my canceled wedding.” Saturday often includes a stop at Ferris Deli, where Amira asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I gave him my old cuff button. It got me through the interview that paid for my divorce.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a narrow-striped sweater and a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges. Amira has a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth, with a blunt cut just below the ears. Amira listens with the head tilted a little to the left during a conversation.
personality: Amira thinks best while walking. Sitting beneath someone's office clock makes Amira sound more certain than they feel, an effect close friends have learned to distrust.
agenda: To get the cuff button back if the applicant decides to change jobs.
family: Naomi Jones is Amira’s cousin raised in the same household. Amira chooses an ordinary story to tell. Naomi asks the question the rest of the family avoided. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *Two names on the chart*, Naomi says, “I am her grown daughter. Reading the childhood name made me realize she was someone before she became Mum.”
connections: Grey Foster. The donated button makes sense to the tailor who left cloth for growth.

reactions.response: Amira checks which part of the jacket can be finished in the time available.

reactions.situation: The last bus leaves while an elderly stranger is still crossing toward it
reactions.response: Amira asks the stranger who will be expecting them, then helps find a way to tell that person.
